reports.title: UNLOCK THE SKIES Q3 2026 SHAREHOLDER LETTER | 1 Q3 2026

desk.headline: Revenue of $5.1m beat as loss widened to $274.6m; Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss seen at $185–205m

other.label: Adjusted EBITDA
other.change: vs -$116.1m a year ago; guided -$170m to -$200m

results: Revenue was $5.1m, ahead of the $3.6m estimate, helped by first engine deliveries to Anduril.
Net loss more than doubled from a year ago to $274.6m ($0.35 a share) as R&D rose to $198.3m.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $178.5m was at the better end of the $170–200m guided range.
Cash and short-term investments fell $207m in the quarter to $1.35bn.

guidance.summary: Archer expects Q4 revenue of $5–6m and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $185–205m, a bit larger than Q3's loss.

points: Only one of nearly 20 approvals remains for buying Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid from Boeing; closing is expected well before year-end.
Insitu brings over $200m of yearly drone revenue, which Archer aims to grow in 2027 to offset Midnight spending.
An FAA certificate clears Midnight flights in Los Angeles within weeks, ahead of LA28 Olympic passenger plans.
Midnight is in the final phase of FAA type certification; piloted transition flight is targeted by year-end.
The hybrid Halo/Thunder aircraft with Anduril remains on track for first full-scale flight in late 2027.
call.source: Shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1); call coverage — Stocktwits, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Closing of the Boeing deal and how fast Insitu revenue grows.
Completion of piloted transition flight and progress on FAA type certification.
Cash burn against $1.35bn of cash and investments.
